blocks.heading: Both steps together, because one without the other does half the job
blocks.body: The serum works on pigment; the cream repairs and seals it in. Bought separately they come to 1,680,000₫. Together the duo is 1,050,000₫, with the SPF50 sunscreen and cleanser included.

blocks.heading: Why dark spots fade and then come straight back
quotes: “Three different serums, and each one worked for about a fortnight.”
“Foundation doesn't really cover the patches on my cheeks.”
“I've been burned by a cream that turned out to have steroids in it.”
“Everything promises results in seven days and nothing delivers.”

explainer.heading: Most products only work on the surface layer
body: Brightening the epidermis alone leaves the melanocytes underneath doing exactly what they were doing before. Stop using the product and the pigment returns, sometimes darker than it started.
This routine takes a different route: it limits the signal that triggers pigment production, supports the turnover of discoloured cells, and rebuilds the skin barrier so the improvement holds.

Which also means progress is measured in weeks, not days. The realistic timelines for each type of discolouration are further down this page, because setting the wrong expectation is how people end up disappointed.

blocks.heading: Three patterns of hyperpigmentation, and honest timelines
blocks.intro: Knowing which one you have tells you what to expect. This is why we do not quote a single number for everybody.

items.heading: Epidermal patches
items.body: Light to dark brown patches with defined edges, sitting in the upper layer. Usually linked to UV exposure, hormonal change, or a previous steroid cream.

image.alt: Light brown patches with defined edges across the cheekbone

items.heading: Dermal pigmentation
items.body: Grey-brown spots or patches with soft edges, where pigment sits deeper in the skin. Linked to genetics, hormones, sun exposure and prolonged stress.

items.heading: Mixed pigmentation
items.body: Both at once: clearly defined dark areas alongside diffuse, patchy ones. It takes longer and demands stricter sun protection.

image.alt: Mixed pigmentation with both defined and diffuse areas

blocks.heading: Four steps, about five minutes
blocks.intro: Once or twice daily. The morning sunscreen is not optional — skip it and the other two steps are largely wasted.

items.heading: Cleanse
items.body: Wash with the Bio-Active Cleanser and pat dry with a clean towel.

items.heading: Serum
items.body: Three to four drops over the affected areas and the whole face. Press in, don't rub.

items.heading: Cream
items.body: About a fingertip's worth across face and neck, avoiding the eye area.

items.heading: Sunscreen
items.body: Every morning, without exception, using the SPF50 included in the duo.

blocks.footnote: Recommended run: 8–12 weeks without gaps. Unprotected sun exposure brings pigment back regardless of which product you use.

items.a: The Smart Brightening Cream X3 and Smart First Care Serum together are 1,050,000₫ (about US$40), including the SPF50 sunscreen and cleanser. Individually: cream 590,000₫, serum 550,000₫.

items.q: How long before I see a difference?
items.a: Most people report a more even-looking tone at four to six weeks of consistent use. Surface patches tend to shift in 4–8 weeks; deeper and mixed pigmentation takes 8–16 weeks. This varies between individuals and depends heavily on daily sun protection.

items.q: Is it suitable for sensitive skin?
items.a: The formula uses Bakuchiol rather than retinol and contains no corticosteroids, hydroquinone or drying alcohol. Patch test on the jawline for 24 hours before applying to the whole face.

items.q: Can I use it while pregnant or breastfeeding?
items.a: The formula is retinoid-free. Even so, speak to your doctor before adding any new product to your routine during pregnancy or breastfeeding.
Pigmentation returns readily when skin is exposed to UV without protection. Completing the 8–12 week run and wearing sunscreen every morning is what makes the improvement hold.
